author: geodro
body:
## Summary

Patch release stacking seven fixes around container-to-host routing, bind-mount lifecycle, and UI state propagation.

- **`lerd.localhost` 504 on rootless Linux**. Dashboard vhost switched from TCP `host.containers.internal:7073` (unreliable on setups where netavark resolves to `169.254.1.2` without DNAT) to a unix socket bind-mounted into `lerd-nginx`. macOS keeps the TCP path since unix sockets don't traverse the podman-machine virtio-fs boundary.
- **Xdebug silent timeouts** (same class as #186). `DetectHostGatewayIP` now runs a real TCP reachability probe against lerd-ui:7073 instead of trusting whatever `getent` returned. `lerd doctor` surfaces failures under a new `[Container → Host connectivity]` section.
- **Coffee-shop laptop regression**. `lerd-watcher` reprobes on primary-LAN-IP change and rewrites `/etc/hosts` in place. Steady-state cost is a single UDP routing-table lookup per tick (no packets sent), only pays for a `podman exec` on an actual network rotation. Matters most on macOS where `podman exec` through gvproxy is 300 ms to 1 s per call.
- **Podman auto-creates a directory at missing bind-mount sources**. `EnsureXdebugIni`, `EnsureUserIni`, and the extracted `ensureFPMHostsFile` now detect and remove stale directories before writing. `WriteContainerHosts` and `writeBrowserHosts` also `MkdirAll` their parent defensively.
- **Dashboard shows stale state after `lerd stop`**. `/api/internal/notify` now refreshes `podman.Cache` before broadcasting, matching the in-process `AfterUnitChange` hook. State flips within a second instead of up to 60 s.

Ships two new tests files (`ini_race_test.go`, `host_gateway_test.go`) plus additions to `manager_test.go`, `remote_control_test.go`, and `hosts_test.go`. Total ~20 new table-driven test cases.

author: ryanrozich
body:
## Summary

Phase 4 poll loop previously only raised attention for DIRTY/BEHIND merge states. For the more common OPEN/BLOCKED case (unresolved review threads or REVIEW_REQUIRED), it did nothing and PRs sat stuck with zombie workers until human intervention.

Adds `plugins/dev/scripts/orchestrate-auto-fixup` which the orchestrator invokes alongside `orchestrate-revive`. It walks non-terminal worker signals, queries `gh pr view` for merge state and `gh api graphql` for review threads, classifies the BLOCKED reason (checks-failing vs threads-unresolved vs review-required), and either auto-dispatches a fix-up worker via `orchestrate-fixup --dispatch` or raises an attention item.

Stability is enforced via a configurable `blockedSince` window (default 10 min) so transient BLOCKED states don't trigger dispatches, and a `fixupAttempts` counter caps auto-dispatches at 2 before escalating to `fixup-budget-exhausted`.

## New signal fields (all nullable, additive)

- `blockedSince` — first observation the PR entered BLOCKED; cleared on exit
- `fixupAttempts` — count of auto-dispatches so far
- `lastFixupDispatchedAt` — telemetry for dashboard / monitor

## Tests

37 shell tests in `__tests__/orchestrate-auto-fixup.test.sh` using stub gh + stub orchestrate-fixup (Wave 3 convention). All pass. No regressions in existing shell test suites.

Closes CTL-64.

This reverts commit 1604bc335157be9a131e24cfde55cab3c90ebc92.

Unfortunately, this commit introduced a regression that causes programs using `spawn_blocking` to hang (see #8056). To fix the regression, we need to undo this change and publish a v1.52.1 release as soon as possible.

In the future, we may wish to bring back a sharded queue for `spawn_blocking` tasks, either based on the implementation added in #7757 or a new one. However, since this is a substantial change to the runtime internals, I think such a change should probably be done as an unstable, opt-in `tokio::runtime::Builder` setting initially, so that we don't regress existing users. I had hoped we could do this now, but unfortunately, the sharded queue implementation from #7757 is kind of tightly coupled with the rest of the `spawn_blocking` machinery and cannot be easily swapped out --- and the hang still occurs with `NUM_SHARDS` set to 1, so there isn't an easy way to turn it on and off. Therefore, in the interest of getting a fix out ASAP, this is just a simple revert.

Fixes #8056

author: hichamboushaba
body:
### Description
Fixes WOOMOB-2723

When a merchant hides a Woo store from the **Edit Stores** screen, this PR unregisters its Woo push token so the device stops receiving notifications for that store. When a previously hidden store is made visible again, its Woo push token is re-registered (gated by `WOO_SELF_DRIVEN_PUSH_NOTIFICATIONS_M1`).

### How it works

The save flow in `WooSitesVisibilityViewModel.performSave` runs sequentially:

1. Unregister Woo push for newly hidden sites (best-effort).
2. Register Woo push for newly visible sites (without WPCom fallback). This internally disables WPCom notifications for those sites. Step 2 tolerates 404 `rest_no_route`, treating sites without the `wc-push-notifications` endpoint as WPCom-only.
3. Update WPCom notification settings, excluding sites currently on Woo push (re-read after step 2 to include sites just registered).

Running register before the WPCom update avoids a race where the WPCom update could re-enable notifications on a site that step 2 just disabled them for.

### Error semantics

| Operation | On failure |
|---|---|
| Unregister Woo push | Best-effort: logged, save continues |
| Register Woo push — site lacks `wc-push-notifications` (404 `rest_no_route`) | Silently skipped, site stays on WPCom, save continues |
| Register Woo push — other errors | Error dialog, save returns early, visibility **not** persisted |
| WPCom settings update | Error dialog, visibility **not** persisted |

### Test Steps

Setup:
- Enable `WOO_SELF_DRIVEN_PUSH_NOTIFICATIONS_M1`.
- Log into an account with 2+ Woo stores; let push registration run.
- Open Logcat with the `NOTIFICATIONS` tag and/or attach a proxy (Proxyman/Charles) to inspect network traffic.

Relevant endpoints:
- Register: `POST /wc-push-notifications/push-tokens`
- Unregister: `DELETE /wc-push-notifications/push-tokens/<tokenId>`
- WPCom settings: `POST /rest/v1.1/me/notifications/settings/`

1. **Hide a Woo-push-registered store.** **Edit Stores** → hide the store → **Save**.
    - Logcat: `Woo Core push token deleted for site <siteId>`.
    - Network: `DELETE /wc-push-notifications/push-tokens/<tokenId>` for that site.
    - No `POST /rest/v1.1/me/notifications/settings/` call is made for that site (it's excluded).
2. **Unhide the same store.** **Edit Stores** → unhide → **Save**.
    - Network: `POST /wc-push-notifications/push-tokens` for that site.
    - Logcat: `WPCom notifications disabled for site <siteId>` (side effect of register).
    - The site is not included in the subsequent `/rest/v1.1/me/notifications/settings/` payload.
3. **Toggle visibility on a store *without* Woo push.** Hide/unhide → **Save**.
    - Network: `POST /rest/v1.1/me/notifications/settings/` with that `blog_id` and the expected `new_comment`/`store_order` flags.
    - On unhide, a `POST /wc-push-notifications/push-tokens` may be attempted and return 404 `rest_no_route` — this is tolerated; the save still succeeds and the site is included in the WPCom settings payload.
4. **Register failure.** Simulate a non-404 failure on `POST /wc-push-notifications/push-tokens` (proxy rewrite or toggle airplane mode after unhide + save).
    - Error dialog shown.
    - No `/rest/v1.1/me/notifications/settings/` call is made after the failure.
    - Visibility is not persisted (reopen the screen; the hidden store is still hidden).
5. **Unregister failure.** Simulate a failure on `DELETE /wc-push-notifications/push-tokens/<tokenId>`.
    - Logcat: `Failed to delete push token for site <siteId>: ...`
    - Save still succeeds and visibility is persisted.

## Summary

- Adds **Clone private to public** as a new menu option (option 3, between "Clone all repos" and "Create a repo")
- Displays all private repos in a numbered list with language and last-pushed date
- User selects a repo and provides a name for the new public repo (defaults to `{original-name}-public`)
- Creates the destination repo via the GitHub API (public, copies description)
- Uses `git clone --mirror` + `git push --mirror` to transfer all branches, tags, and full commit history
- Rolls back the newly created repo if the clone step fails, leaving no orphaned repos
- Updates README with the new feature

- [ ] Run `python main.py` and verify "Clone private to public" appears in the menu
- [ ] Verify only private repos are listed (no public repos shown)
- [ ] Select a repo, accept the default name, confirm the new public repo is created on GitHub with full history
- [ ] Select a repo, enter a custom name, verify it is used

- Reworked the frontend `App.jsx` into a connector-first console with source-aware account badges, a connector management panel, manual account creation, manual trade entry, and a JSON-based CSV import flow. (`frontend/src/App.jsx`).

- Harmonize bottom navigation across category and special screens so items open the dedicated activities instead of routing through `MainActivity` with flags.
- Standardize bookmark and share icons/behaviour across lists and sliders to use consistent assets and immediate UI feedback after save/remove.
- Surface author/date in dossier slider and adjust slider/card/layout sizing for better visuals.

- Updated Android navigation: bottom nav handlers in `AlaUneActivity`, `CategoryNewsActivity`, `FavorisActivity`, `PlusLusActivity` and `HomeTnActivity` now open `FavorisActivity`, `PlusLusActivity` or `HomeTnActivity` directly as appropriate and set the selected item state in favorites/top24 screens.

author: hopeatina
body:
## The bug (observed in Claude)

**morning-brief renders completely blank** and **agent-status's metric rail stacks vertically** instead of the 4-column grid.

## Root cause

Both widgets used `@import url('./shared/tokens.css')` inside an inline `<style>` block. The MCP Apps serving pipeline URL-rewrites attribute values (\`href\`, \`src\`, \`srcset\`, \`poster\`) but explicitly skips the interior of `<style>` and `<script>` blocks. Result: the relative `./shared/tokens.css` stayed relative, Claude's sandbox couldn't resolve it against the `ui://` resource, and tokens.css never loaded.

- `.app-metric-rail { display: grid }` lives in tokens.css → agent-status metrics stacked as block-level divs.
- morning-brief depends on tokens.css for every color variable → rendered invisible-on-dark.

## The fix (three layers)

1. **Widgets pull tokens via `<link>`** instead of `@import` — `<link href>` values DO get URL-rewritten and survive the sandbox.
2. **Runtime inlines `shared/tokens.css`** — added to `MCP_APPS_SHARED_COMPONENT_PATHS`. Even if a future widget reintroduces the issue, the content gets inlined directly.
3. **Build-time lint blocks reintroduction** — `scripts/build-widgets.mjs` gains `validateNoSharedAtImport`. Any `@import url(...)` pointing into `shared/` inside a `<style>` block fails the build with a pointed error.

## Symmetry invariant added

The build now cross-checks: every `RUNTIME_INLINED_PATHS` entry must be on `SHARED_ALLOWLIST` AND must be referenced by at least one widget. Catches the dead-inlining-logic class of bug both directions.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 211/211 pass
- [x] Lint caught live: temporarily reintroducing `@import` fails the build with the right error
- [ ] Visual: `/widgets/morning-brief.html?demo=true` in Claude sandbox now renders fully styled
- [ ] Visual: `/widgets/agent-status.html?demo=true` shows 4-column metric rail

author: dtamayo-nlp
body:
**Motivation**

Previous implementation worked correctly for SFT, but did not scale to pre-training workloads and eventually led to NCCL timeouts under tests with 4000 files and billions of tokens.

**Features Introduced**

The main bottleneck was the packing stage:

- bisect.insort() incurs O(N) insertion cost, making the overall complexity O(N log N + NxB), which degrades to ~O(N^2) for large corpora (N = number of documents, B = number of bins). Replacing it with SortedList reduced insertion to O(log N) and improved the complexity to O(N log N), but Python overhead remained a bottleneck at scale.
To fully address this, the default implementation was changed to C++ (python implementation is still available).

To correctly adapt the pipeline for pre-training, the following changes were also introduced:

- Chunking instead of truncation: documents longer than seq_len are split into fixed-length chunks prior to packing. For SFT-derived fragments missing a valid BOS/context, all turns (<|system_start|> ... <|assistant_end|>) are masked to avoid learning from incomplete contexts.
- Support for mixed data regimes: the pipeline now handles both SFT and raw pre-training data. Sub-documents without `<|system_start|>`,`<|developer_start|>` or `<|user_start|>` are treated as pure pre-training samples and incur full loss without masking.

**Tests done**:
- Large run with pre-training + SFT synthetic long context samples: Gives best performance on RULER while keeping the same short context performance. Speed is similar.
- Tests with SFT samples with sample_length > seq_length: The loss is correctly masked.

**Observation on Packing Efficiency**

When most documents are already close to seq_len, best-fit packing becomes inefficient. In the current long-context setting, I regenerated the dataset with a wider length distribution, which significantly improved bin-packing efficiency. This is an important consideration for future dataset construction.

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
This pull request introduces a major architectural shift to an **Agent-First Code Review Engine (V3)**, replacing the previous single-shot LLM approach with an active, tool-using agentic workflow. It also integrates AST-based call graphs, robust BYOK concurrency management, and a completely revamped evaluation and benchmarking suite.

### Core Changes

*   **Agent-First Review Engine (V3)**:
    *   Introduced `CodeReviewAgentPipelineStrategy` and `AgentReviewStage` to orchestrate the new review process.
    *   Implemented specialized agents (`BugAgentProvider`, `SecurityAgentProvider`, `PerformanceAgentProvider`, `GeneralistAgentProvider`, and `KodyRulesAgentProvider`) that actively investigate the codebase using tools (`grep`, `readFile`, `listDir`, `checkTypes`, `readReference`) inside a secure sandbox before making suggestions.
    *   Added `BusinessLogicValidationStage` as a distinct, top-level pipeline stage to validate PR descriptions against business requirements.
*   **AST Call Graph Integration**:
    *   Integrated `kodus-graph` to build and incrementally update AST-based call graphs for repositories.
    *   Added database migrations and TypeORM models (`AstNodeModel`, `AstEdgeModel`, `RepositoryModel`) to persist graph data.
    *   Implemented `AstGraphBuildJobProcessor` and `AstGraphIncrementalJobProcessor` to handle full and incremental graph builds in the background, triggered by GitHub `push` events.
    *   Replaced the legacy `CodeAstAnalysisService` and `ASTContentFormatterService` with the new `GraphContextService` and `GraphContentFormatter`.
*   **BYOK Concurrency & Reasoning Support**:
    *   Added `ByokConcurrencyGateService` using PostgreSQL advisory locks to strictly enforce `maxConcurrentRequests` for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) LLM configurations, preventing rate-limit exhaustion.
    *   Updated BYOK settings in the Web UI and backend to support configuring `reasoningEffort` and `reasoningConfigOverride` for advanced models (e.g., Claude 3.7 extended thinking, OpenAI o-series).
*   **Evaluation & Benchmarking**:
    *   Removed the legacy `promptfoo` and `cross-file` evaluation suites.
    *   Introduced new `investigation` and `promotion` evaluation suites to separately measure the agent's codebase exploration and its decision-making accuracy.
    *   Added a comprehensive benchmark pipeline (`scripts/benchmark/*`) to evaluate the engine against the `withmartian` code review dataset (50 PRs, 136 golden comments).
*   **Web UI Enhancements**:
    *   Updated the PR timeline (`PrListItem`) to display detailed agent traces, including tool call summaries and execution durations.
    *   Adapted the "Suggestion Control" (now "Review Filters") settings page to support the `v3-agent` version, removing obsolete grouping modes.
    *   Refined the Kody Rules library UI to use severity levels instead of MCP plugin filters.
*   **Sandbox & Infrastructure**:
    *   Enhanced `LocalSandboxService` to support `exec` with a strict whitelist of read-only programs (e.g., `tsc`, `eslint`, `cargo check`, `ast-grep`) for local type-checking and linting.
    *   Updated `E2BSandboxService` to fetch the base branch, enabling `git diff` operations inside the sandbox.
    *   Eagerly declared RabbitMQ delayed exchanges and Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) in `RabbitMQDLQInitializer` to prevent message loss on startup.

## Pipeline
```
app/data/scams/*.json  +  book/manuscript/*.md  →  Pandoc  →  book/build/japan-scams.epub
```

Single command:
```bash
pip3 install pyyaml
```

- Title page + copyright/disclaimer

- **Six universal red-flag patterns** (~2,000 words — the highest-value differentiating chapter)

author: echeresh
body:
PR fixes [MFDNN-14864](https://jira.devtools.intel.com/browse/MFDNN-14864).

## Background

According to the [documentation](https://uxlfoundation.github.io/oneDNN/dev_guide_attributes_accumulation_mode.html), oneDNN must use an f32 accumulator with f16 data type inputs. GPU convolution deviates from that in some cases due to historical and performance reasons:

-	f16 small-channel convolution (including depthwise) may use mad instructions with a half-precision accumulator for better performance. Why: systolic uses an f32 accumulator but requires larger chains: 16 elements per reduction, which adds extra overhead.
-	Xe-LP(G) platforms may use an f16 accumulator for f16 inputs in convolution. Why: no systolic support, and f32 accumulator mad has 2x lower throughput.

PR fixes this mismatch by switching to an f32 accumulator with f16 data types in GPU convolution by default. The driver of this change is the recent bug report about poor f16 accuracy in convolution: [MFDNN-14864](https://jira.devtools.intel.com/browse/MFDNN-14864).

## Impact
- Accuracy: improved on the affected paths
- Performance: default f16 convolution may be slower than before. This is relevant for depthwise and small-channel f16 shapes for forward and backward by data.
    - oneDNN performance testing shows up to ~20% E2E regressions; however, these are limited to ~10 KPIs out of hundreds tracked. Individual layers show regressions up to 2x.

## Mitigation: how to opt in to the old (faster) behavior

Set the accumulation_mode primitive attribute to any:

```c++
attr.set_accumulation_mode(dnnl::accumulation_mode::any);
```

No code changes are needed beyond setting the attribute on convolution primitives where reduced-precision accumulation is acceptable.

author: apexbusiness-systems
body:
## Summary

This PR adds critical reliability fixes to the WhepPlayer component and introduces a CORS probe utility to surface actionable errors when WHEP endpoints are misconfigured. It also includes comprehensive regression test suites for both the player and URL detection logic.

## Key Changes

### WhepPlayer Component Fixes
- **Fix #1**: Collapsed dual retry paths into a single `scheduleRetry()` call to prevent duplicate retry timers from accumulating during bursty no-media events
- **Fix #3**: Extracted `manualRetry` callback to eliminate stale closure issues when users click "Retry now" after max retries exceeded
- **Fix #4**: Added `mountedRef` guard to prevent state updates after component unmount; explicitly null ICE handler on destroy to prevent late state-change events from firing into stale closures
- **Fix #5**: Added `clearRetryTimer()` utility and `connectingRef` guard to prevent zombie retry timers from tearing down healthy streams after ICE recovery or media recovery; clears pending retry when ICE transitions to 'connected'/'completed' or when 'media-recovered' event fires
- **CORS Probe**: Integrated pre-flight CORS check via `probeWhepCors()` to surface specific, actionable error hints (e.g., missing Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers) instead of generic "Failed to fetch" messages

### New Utilities
- **`whep-probe.ts`**: Lightweight pre-flight probe for WHEP endpoints that detects CORS blocks, network unreachability, DNS failures, and timeouts with operator-friendly hints. Non-blocking by design—probe failures are advisory and do not prevent playback attempts
- **`url-detector.ts` enhancements** (Fix #2): Improved WHEP URL detection to recognize `/whep/` as a standalone path segment (not substring matches like `/badwhep/`); correctly classifies all `*.sbbl-hq.icu` subdomains

### Test Coverage
- **`whep-player.test.tsx`**: Comprehensive regression suite covering all 5 critical fixes plus CORS probe integration, including:
  - Mount/unmount lifecycle and state update guards
  - Retry deduplication under bursty no-media events
  - Manual retry button behavior and retry count reset
  - ICE recovery and media recovery clearing pending timers
  - CORS error surfacing with actionable hints
  
- **`url-detector.test.ts`**: Full coverage of stream type detection including WHEP path segment validation, platform detection (YouTube, Twitch, HLS, DASH, etc.), and advisory messaging

- **`whep-probe.test.ts`**: Probe result taxonomy covering reachability, CORS blocks, network errors, timeouts, and invalid URLs with mocked fetch implementations

## Implementation Details

- Uses `mountedRef` to guard all state updates and callbacks, preventing memory leaks and stale closures after unmount
- `connectingRef` prevents overlapping concurrent `connect()` invocations that could stack up multiple WebRTCPlayer instances
- Exponential backoff with jitter on retry to prevent thundering herd on broadcaster restart
- CORS probe uses OPTIONS preflight with configurable timeout; treats 405/501 responses as acceptable (server is reachable, real POST preflight will be checked by player)
- All timers and event handlers are explicitly cleaned up on destroy to prevent resource leaks

This pull request introduces several improvements to camera behavior and rendering performance, particularly by making the camera smoothly follow the player with a "deadzone," and optimizing world and pheromone rendering to only draw visible tiles. It also refactors function signatures to support these changes and tightens up the visibility update logic.

**Camera and Rendering Improvements:**

* Added smooth camera following with a configurable deadzone and lerp speed, ensuring the camera only moves when the player leaves a central area, and clamps camera position to the map bounds. (`src/main.c`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e0cf5b28d9b6b600f0af2bc78e8fd30ec675fd731a5da86f0c4283ffc0e40176L181-R185) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e0cf5b28d9b6b600f0af2bc78e8fd30ec675fd731a5da86f0c4283ffc0e40176R223-R243)
* Changed camera initialization and update logic to center the camera on the screen and removed dynamic zooming to fit the map, instead using a fixed zoom value. (`src/main.c`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e0cf5b28d9b6b600f0af2bc78e8fd30ec675fd731a5da86f0c4283ffc0e40176L181-R185) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e0cf5b28d9b6b600f0af2bc78e8fd30ec675fd731a5da86f0c4283ffc0e40176L238-R268)

**Rendering Optimization:**

* Updated `WorldDraw` and `Pheromone_Draw` to accept a `Camera2D*` parameter and only render tiles within the camera's view, improving performance on large maps. (`src/world.c`, `src/world.h`, `src/main.c`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6987e9c2dc487ffd3cef54a542070a1c3e8d92d6da18e59966cc89db0ea1aeedL139-R168) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6987e9c2dc487ffd3cef54a542070a1c3e8d92d6da18e59966cc89db0ea1aeedL191-R233) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3eff6858828354c1828bd9569e90c438b9580dc273450d449538c71795f8d0eeL40-R46) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-e0cf5b28d9b6b600f0af2bc78e8fd30ec675fd731a5da86f0c4283ffc0e40176L238-R268)

**Visibility System Refinement:**

* Optimized the area affected by visibility decay and update, focusing calculations around the player and ensuring bounds are properly clamped. (`src/world.c`)

**API Changes:**

* Updated function signatures for `WorldDraw` and `Pheromone_Draw` to include the camera, requiring changes at call sites. (`src/world.h`, `src/main.c`, `src/world.c`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3eff6858828354c1828bd9569e90c438b9580dc273450d449538c71795f8d0eeL40-R46) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e0cf5b28d9b6b600f0af2bc78e8fd30ec675fd731a5da86f0c4283ffc0e40176L238-R268) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6987e9c2dc487ffd3cef54a542070a1c3e8d92d6da18e59966cc89db0ea1aeedL139-R168) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6987e9c2dc487ffd3cef54a542070a1c3e8d92d6da18e59966cc89db0ea1aeedL191-R233)

Performance Impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Tile draws (max map) | 14,400 | ~800 |
| Visibility decay | Full map | ~2x view radius |
| Draw calls | ~10K+ | ~2K max |

These changes collectively make camera movement smoother and more intuitive, and significantly improve rendering efficiency by only drawing what is visible to the player.Introduce smooth camera movement with lerp and deadzone. author: ziggie1984
body:
## Problem

When a peer rejects our `CommitSig` with an `Error` message, the
`InvalidCommitSigError` it sends back contains the commitment
transaction the peer built on their side (logged via the existing error
handling). We never logged the commitment transaction **we** signed,
making it impossible to determine whether the failure was caused by a
state divergence (the two peers derived different transactions) or a
genuine signing bug.

This gap was observed in a CI failure on
[#10628](https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/10628)
([run](https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/actions/runs/24372618188/job/71461112768):
the `zero_conf-channel_policy_update_public_zero_conf` itest got stuck
with a payment `IN_FLIGHT` due to an `InvalidCommitSigError` at
`commit_height=5` on Carol's side. Carol's `commit_tx` was visible in
the error log, but Dave's was not, leaving the root cause unresolvable.

## Solution

Add `BuildLastSignedRemoteCommitTx` to `LightningChannel`. The method
re-derives the commitment transaction most recently signed for the
remote party by mirroring the exact index snapshot used in
`SignNextCommitment`. It must be called before a subsequent
`RevokeAndAck` from the remote rotates `RemoteNextRevocation` to a new
commitment point (which is guaranteed on the error path since the peer
sends `Error` instead of `RevokeAndAck`).

`processRemoteError` in the htlcswitch now calls this method and logs
the result alongside the peer's error. Comparing the two `commit_tx`
fields immediately reveals any state divergence without requiring a
live debugger or a second reproduction of the failure.

## Identifying divergence from logs

With this change, a future failure would log:

```
# Carol's side (existing):
invalid_commit_sig commit_tx=<carol_tx> sig_hash=<h> ...

# Dave's side (new):
signer-side commit_tx=<dave_tx> (compare with commit_tx in the peer error above ...)
```

If `<carol_tx> != <dave_tx>` the two peers derived different
transactions from the same state — that is the root cause. If they
match, the signature itself is broken and the sighash / signing path
needs investigation.

## Summary

Three combined changes to the Call Parsing Classify Review workspace, planned and shipped together because they share the same components and data flow.

- **Added events now render their spectrogram region.** `GET /classification-jobs/{id}/typed-events` used to read `events.parquet` directly, so user-added boundary-correction events (`add-` prefix) came back with an empty `region_id` and the frontend couldn't locate their region. - **Non-interactive "None" palette chip.** When the current event has no above-threshold prediction and no correction, the palette shows a disabled-looking "None" chip so the unlabeled state is obvious. The chip stays in the DOM (`visibility: hidden`) when a type is active, so the palette doesn't reflow between events.
- **2-letter type badge on every labeled event bar.** Inference picks render as a colored outline on white (legible against the purple bar); human corrections render as a solid palette-color fill; negative corrections render as a solid red `—`. Unlabeled events get no badge. Bar geometry and drag/resize handlers are unchanged.
- **Palette click no longer toggles off.** Clicking the button matching the current inference prediction now promotes the prediction to a human correction; re-clicking an existing correction is idempotent (doesn't dirty Save).

body:
## Summary

- The security config's auto-disconnect options (`disconnectOnIdle`, `disconnectOnLock`, `disconnectOnSuspend`) silently kicked the user off their session with no indication of why.
- The pieces for a toast were already in place — `backend/lib/security.ts` sends `AppEvent.disconnect` with a reason string, and `LockManager.vue` has a `noty.warning("Disconnected: ${reason}")` handler registered via `$root.$on`.
- The renderer's `AppEventHandler` was the broken link: it caught the IPC event and only dispatched the store action, never forwarding it onto the Vue root bus, so the `LockManager` handler never fired.

This just adds `this.forward(AppEvent.disconnect)` alongside the existing handler so both the store dispatch and the toast run. Menu-driven disconnects still send no reason and `LockManager` bails in that case, so manual disconnects stay quiet.

FYI for anyone reviewing: the idle check is based on `powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime()`, which is true system-wide idle (no keyboard/mouse input anywhere on the OS), not app-focus time.

## Test plan

- [ ] Set `disconnectOnIdle = true` and a short `idleThresholdSeconds` in config, connect to a DB, leave the machine alone, confirm you're disconnected *and* see a "Disconnected: User has been idle" toast.
- [ ] Set `disconnectOnLock = true`, connect, lock the screen, unlock, confirm the "Screen was locked" toast is visible.

## Why

Some of the quick Chainsaw e2e tests appear to fail because the Kubernetes resource reaches `status.ready=true` before the corresponding Linode API read/list endpoint reflects the new object consistently. In practice, the failing pattern is an immediate one-shot `curl` assertion against the provider API returning no result or incomplete linkage right after the controller reports readiness.

This change makes those checks more reliable by adding bounded polling directly inside the existing Chainsaw `script` steps.

## What changed

- add minimal polling loops to the affected provider-facing `curl` checks in the quick suite
- keep shell strictness at `set -e`
- move the affected checks to `https://api.linode.com/v4beta/...`
- fix the VPC delete validation to query the VPC endpoint instead of the nodebalancer endpoint

## Scope

This is intentionally a minimal test hardening change.

- no controller logic changes
